pipelines.summary: Successfully implemented frontend types and API client for class-range feature. Added classRangeApi.calculate() to api.ts service, calling POST /calculate/class-range endpoint. comments.note: Types were already present in physics.d.ts — this suggests the files were updated in parallel or by a previous work session. Verified all types match backend DTOs exactly.
useClassRange hook follows the exact pattern of usePhysicsCalculation — excellent consistency. Same state structure, debounce approach, cleanup pattern.
Debounce at 500ms for class-range vs 300ms for single-ship is appropriate given the heavier backend computation (~80 ships vs 1). Comment in hook code explains the reasoning.
api.ts: Timeout is hardcoded at 10000ms (10s). For class-range calculations with many ships, this might be tight if backend exceeds 100ms target significantly. Consider making timeout configurable.

pipelines.summary: WP-003 PASSED QA validation. All 9 acceptance criteria met. Frontend types match backend DTOs, API client and hook work correctly, 500ms debounce implemented. No npm dependencies added. Note: Some types were pre-existing from prior work, but all match backend contracts. Ready for code review.

comments.description: TypeScript interfaces match backend DTOs exactly. All properties properly typed with correct optional/nullable handling (e.g., 'topSpeed?: number | null'). Excellent type safety.
classRangeApi.calculate() follows established pattern from physicsApi.calculate(). Proper error handling with try-catch. Hardcoded timeout (10000ms) is documented with comment explaining reasoning.

GOLD NUGGET: Timeout is hardcoded at 10s. For class-range calculations with 80+ ships, this might be tight if backend exceeds 100ms target. Consider making timeout configurable per endpoint (e.g., 10s for single-ship, 15s for class-range).

Hook follows exact pattern of usePhysicsCalculation - excellent consistency. useState for result/loading/error, useCallback for calculate/reset, useRef for debounce timer. Cleanup on unmount handles timer properly.
500ms debounce (vs 300ms for single-ship) is well-reasoned given heavier backend computation. Comment explicitly explains this choice. Good documentation of design decisions.
Debounce timer cleanup in useEffect return function prevents memory leaks. Proper React hook lifecycle management.
Loading state set immediately before debounce timer starts. This provides instant user feedback ('loading' state) even though API call is 500ms delayed. Good UX pattern.
No security concerns. TypeScript type safety prevents type confusion attacks. No eval or code execution. API calls use fetch with proper error handling.
All TypeScript code compiles under strict mode. No 'any' types. Proper use of interfaces and type annotations throughout.

gold_nuggets: Make API timeout configurable per endpoint (10s for single-ship, 15s for class-range) to handle varying backend computation times
Consider extracting debounce logic into reusable useDebounce hook to reduce duplication between usePhysicsCalculation and useClassRange
